what_it_shows: Base58Check version 0x00: the Bitcoin P2PKH string is also the legacy-format Bitcoin Cash address of the same hash. Nothing in the string says which chain it is for.
source: Bitcoin genesis-block address (Bitcoin Wiki); CashAddr specification, legacy format

what_it_shows: Base58Check version 0x05: a Bitcoin P2SH address is byte-identical to a legacy Litecoin P2SH address (version 5, SCRIPT_ADDRESS) and to a legacy Bitcoin Cash P2SH address.
source: Bitcoin Wiki Address page; Litecoin Core chainparams.cpp and key_io.cpp; CashAddr specification
notes: Litecoin also uses version 0x32 (M...) for P2SH. A 3... string sent to the wrong chain is a valid address there, controlled by the holder of the script.

what_it_shows: A lower-case 0x + 40 hex string is an EVM address (no checksum asserted) and a NEAR Ethereum-like account ID.
source: EIP-55 test case in lower case; NEAR documentation, Ethereum-like address

what_it_shows: The Solana system program id (32 zero bytes in Base58) is also a well-formed NEAR account ID (32 digits).
A lower-case Bitcoin Bech32 address satisfies the NEAR account ID grammar (lower-case letters and digits, 42 characters).
notes: An application that accepts a NEAR account ID after a Bitcoin address was pasted into the wrong field cannot tell from the string alone.

what_it_shows: A CashAddr without its prefix is a well-formed NEAR account ID.
source: CashAddr specification example without prefix; near-account-id-rs validation rules

what_it_shows: Upper-case hex digits are valid for EVM but not for NEAR (account IDs are lower case), so this string is not ambiguous with NEAR.
64 lower-case hex digits: a NEAR implicit account ID and also the usual hex form of a 32-byte Ed25519 public key; it contains 0 and is not Base58, so it is not a Solana address.
source: RFC 8032 section 7.1 test 1 public key; NEAR documentation, implicit address

what_it_shows: The same 20-byte hash160 of the Bitcoin genesis-block address appears under seven address encodings: the strings differ, the bytes are the same. Whoever holds the key for one holds it for all of them.
source: Bitcoin Wiki Genesis block page; the encodings of each family
notes: A different version byte or alphabet is the only thing separating them; Base58Check detects a wrong version only if the receiver checks it.

what_it_shows: The 32-byte Ed25519 public key of RFC 8032 test 1 as a TON raw account id, a NEAR implicit account, a Solana address and a Stellar account ID.
notes: A TON account id is a contract-state hash, not a public key; the raw form is only used here as a 32-byte container.

what_it_shows: The 20 bytes after the 41 prefix of a TRON hex address are the Ethereum-form address; TRON documentation says so.
notes: The 0x-prefixed string with upper-case letters and no lower-case letters is a valid EVM string (single case).

what_it_shows: Same 20 bytes, two checksum conventions: the capitalisation above is the EIP-1191 checksum for chain id 30 (RSK mainnet); it is not the EIP-55 capitalisation, so an EIP-55 validator rejects it.
notes: The lower-case form of the same bytes is valid EVM (no checksum asserted).
